Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 44, verse 1–16:

Makkiyya (Meccan), and it has fifty-nine verses, three hundred and forty-six words, and one thousand, four hundred and eighty-one letters.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed us: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah related to us: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan related to us: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us: Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us: Abu Isa ibn Ali al-Khutali related to us: Abu Hashim al-Rifa'i related to us: Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us: Umar ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Sarri related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Dukhan on a night, seventy thousand angels will seek forgiveness for him by morning." [207] [[Sunan al-Darimi: 4/237.]]

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed us: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali related to us: al-Sarraj related to us: Abu Yahya related to us: Kathir ibn Hisham related to us, from Hisham ibn al-Miqdam, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ha-Mim, the one in which the smoke is mentioned, on Friday night, will be forgiven by morning." [208] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 11/94.]]

Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Tabarani informed us there: Abu Ali al-Raqqa' related to us: Abu Mansur Sulayman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed us: Talut ibn Abbad related to us: Fadilal ibn Kathir Ha related to us, who said:

I came to Abu Umama, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever recites Ha-Mim al-Dukhan on Friday night, or on Friday, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise." [209] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/168.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ha-Mim. By the Manifest Book. Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We are ever warning. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said:

It is the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr): Allah the Exalted sent down the Qur'an during the Night of Power from the Mother of the Book to the lowest heaven, then He sent it down upon His Prophet (ﷺ) over nights and days. Others said: It is the night of the middle of Sha'ban.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad Fanjawayh informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim related to us: Ibrahim al-Mustamli al-Hastajani related to us: Abu Husayn ibn Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us: Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabra informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Mu'awiya ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, from his father, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban, stand in prayer during its night and fast its day, for indeed Allah, the Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven at sunset and says: 'Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Is there anyone seeking provision, that I may provide for him? Is there anyone afflicted, that I may heal him? Is there anyone afflicted, that I may heal him? Is there such-and-such, is there such-and-such, is there such-and-such,' until the dawn rises." [210] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/314, no. 35177.]]

Indeed, We are ever warning.

Therein is made distinct (yufraqu: yufassalu, is separated). Every wise matter (kullu amrin hakim: muhkam, decreed). Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah said: In the Night of Power in the month of Ramadan, every term, deed, creation and provision is determined, and whatever will happen in that year. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The affairs of the year are arranged on the Night of Power. Hilal ibn Nasaf said: It used to be said: Await the decree in the month of Ramadan.

Ikrimah said: On the night of the middle of Sha'ban, the affairs of the year are decreed in it, the living are separated from the dead, and the pilgrims are recorded, so none is added to them and none is subtracted from them.

Evidence for this is what:

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-Faraj al-Qadi informed us: Muhammad ibn Jubayr informed us: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to me: my father related to me: al-Layth related to us, from Aqil ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab, from Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughira al-Akhnas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Terms are cut off from Sha'ban to Sha'ban, to the extent that a man marries and has children, while his name has already gone out among the dead." [211] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/694, no. 42780.]]

Amran (a command): i.e., We sent down a command. From Our presence (min 'indina): from Our side. Al-Farra' said: It is in the accusative on the meaning of "We distinguish every matter, a distinguishing," and "amran." Indeed, We are ever sending messengers (inna kunna mursilin): Muhammad (ﷺ) to Our servants. As a mercy from your Lord (rahmatan min rabbika): it was said: We sent it down as a mercy; it was said: We sent him as a mercy; and it was said: the mercy.

Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. The people of Kufa read "rabbi" with a kasra (bi') as a response to His words "from your Lord," while others read it with a damma as a response to His words "He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing," and if you wish, it is an inceptive (mubtada').

If you are certain (in kuntum muqinin): indeed Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so be certain that Muhammad is His Messenger and that the Qur'an is His revelation. There is no god but Him; He gives life and causes death. Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones. Rather, they are in doubt, playing. So await (faratqib: fantazir), the day when the heaven brings a manifest smoke.

They differed concerning this smoke: what it is and when it is.

Al-A'mash and Muslim ibn Subayh related from Masruq, who said: We were sitting with Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and he was reclining among us, when a man came to him and said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, a storyteller at the gates of Kinda is telling stories and says, concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: "The day the heaven brings a manifest smoke," that it is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection, which will seize the breaths of the disbelievers and hypocrites, and their hearing and sight, and the believers will be affected by it like a cold. Then Abd Allah stood up and sat down, while angry, and said: O people, fear Allah. Whoever knows something, let him say what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say: Allah knows best. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): "Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not of the pretenders" [Surat Sad: 86]. I will tell you about this: when Quraysh delayed in accepting Islam and persisted in opposing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: "O Allah, seven years like the years of Joseph." [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 14/549, with variation in wording.]] [212] So affliction and hunger befell them, until they ate carrion, bones, dead animals and hides, and they would raise their eyes to the sky and see nothing but smoke, from the darkness of their sight due to the intensity of hunger. Then Abu Sufyan ibn Harb came to him and said: O Muhammad, you command obedience and the keeping of kinship ties, and your people have perished, so invoke Allah for them, for they will obey you.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: They said:

"Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers." So he invoked, and it was removed from them. Allah, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return [to your disbelief]." On the day We seize with the greatest seizure, indeed We will take retribution. So they returned, and Allah took retribution from them on the day of Badr. Thus five have passed: the smoke, the constant punishment, the seizing, the moon, and the Romans.

Others said: Rather, it is a smoke that will come before the Hour, which will enter the hearing of the disbelievers and hypocrites, until it becomes like a roasted head, and the believer among them will be affected like a cold, and the whole earth will be like a house set alight in which there are no gaps.

They said: It has not yet come, but it is coming. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umayr, al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali. Evidence for it is what:

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Asam ibn Dawud al-Jarrah related to us: my father related to us: Sufyan ibn Sa'id related to us: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir related to us, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the signs are the smoke, the descent of Jesus son of Mary, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden in Abyan, driving people to the gathering place, staying with them when they rest." [213] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/259, no. 38645.]]

Hudhayfa said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the smoke? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then recited this verse: "The day the heaven brings a manifest smoke, covering the people; this is a painful punishment" [44:10–11]. It will fill what is between the east and the west, remaining forty days and nights. As for the believer, it will afflict him like a cold; as for the disbeliever, it will be like the state of a drunkard, coming out of his nostrils, ears and rear.

And with this chain from Ibn Jarir: Ya'qub related to us: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulayka, who said: I went to Ibn Abbas one day, and he said: I did not sleep last night until morning. I said: Why? He said: They said: the comet with a tail has risen, and I feared that the smoke had come by night, so I did not sleep until morning.

"Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers." How can they have the reminder (anna lahumu al-dhikra): from where would they have remembrance and admonition after the coming of the trial and the descent of punishment? "And there had already come to them a clear Messenger" (Muhammad, ﷺ). "Then they turned away from him and said: 'Taught, a man is teaching him,' 'a madman.'" "Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return to your disbelief." Qatadah said: "You will return to the punishment of Allah."

"On the day We seize with the greatest seizure": it is the day of Badr. "Indeed We will take retribution": this is the view of most scholars. Al-Hasan said: it is the Day of Resurrection.

It is reported from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "the greatest" is the day of Badr, and I say it is the Day of Resurrection.

Is there such-and-such, is there such-and-such, is there such-and-such,' until the dawn rises." [210] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/314, no. 35177.]]

Indeed, We are ever warning.

Therein is made distinct (yufraqu: yufassalu, is separated). Every wise matter (kullu amrin hakim: muhkam, decreed). Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah said: In the Night of Power in the month of Ramadan, every term, deed, creation and provision is determined, and whatever will happen in that year. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The affairs of the year are arranged on the Night of Power. Hilal ibn Nasaf said: It used to be said: Await the decree in the month of Ramadan.

Ikrimah said: On the night of the middle of Sha'ban, the affairs of the year are decreed in it, the living are separated from the dead, and the pilgrims are recorded, so none is added to them and none is subtracted from them.

Evidence for this is what:

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-Faraj al-Qadi informed us: Muhammad ibn Jubayr informed us: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to me: my father related to me: al-Layth related to us, from Aqil ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab, from Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughira al-Akhnas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Terms are cut off from Sha'ban to Sha'ban, to the extent that a man marries and has children, while his name has already gone out among the dead." [211] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/694, no. 42780.]]

Amran (a command): i.e., We sent down a command. From Our presence (min 'indina): from Our side. Al-Farra' said: It is in the accusative on the meaning of "We distinguish every matter, a distinguishing," and "amran." Indeed, We are ever sending messengers (inna kunna mursilin): Muhammad (ﷺ) to Our servants. As a mercy from your Lord (rahmatan min rabbika): it was said: We sent it down as a mercy; it was said: We sent him as a mercy; and it was said: the mercy.

Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. The people of Kufa read "rabbi" with a kasra (bi') as a response to His words "from your Lord," while others read it with a damma as a response to His words "He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing," and if you wish, it is an inceptive (mubtada').

If you are certain (in kuntum muqinin): indeed Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so be certain that Muhammad is His Messenger and that the Qur'an is His revelation. There is no god but Him; He gives life and causes death. Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones. Rather, they are in doubt, playing. So await (faratqib: fantazir), the day when the heaven brings a manifest smoke.

They differed concerning this smoke: what it is and when it is.

Al-A'mash and Muslim ibn Subayh related from Masruq, who said: We were sitting with Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and he was reclining among us, when a man came to him and said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, a storyteller at the gates of Kinda is telling stories and says, concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: "The day the heaven brings a manifest smoke," that it is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection, which will seize the breaths of the disbelievers and hypocrites, and their hearing and sight, and the believers will be affected by it like a cold. Then Abd Allah stood up and sat down, while angry, and said: O people, fear Allah. Whoever knows something, let him say what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say: Allah knows best. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): "Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not of the pretenders" [Surat Sad: 86]. I will tell you about this: when Quraysh delayed in accepting Islam and persisted in opposing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: "O Allah, seven years like the years of Joseph." [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 14/549, with variation in wording.]] [212] So affliction and hunger befell them, until they ate carrion, bones, dead animals and hides, and they would raise their eyes to the sky and see nothing but smoke, from the darkness of their sight due to the intensity of hunger. Then Abu Sufyan ibn Harb came to him and said: O Muhammad, you command obedience and the keeping of kinship ties, and your people have perished, so invoke Allah for them, for they will obey you.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: They said:

"Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers." So he invoked, and it was removed from them. Allah, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return [to your disbelief]." On the day We seize with the greatest seizure, indeed We will take retribution. So they returned, and Allah took retribution from them on the day of Badr. Thus five have passed: the smoke, the constant punishment, the seizing, the moon, and the Romans.

Others said: Rather, it is a smoke that will come before the Hour, which will enter the hearing of the disbelievers and hypocrites, until it becomes like a roasted head, and the believer among them will be affected like a cold, and the whole earth will be like a house set alight in which there are no gaps.

They said: It has not yet come, but it is coming. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umayr, al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali. Evidence for it is what:

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us: Asam ibn Dawud al-Jarrah related to us: my father related to us: Sufyan ibn Sa'id related to us: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir related to us, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the signs are the smoke, the descent of Jesus son of Mary, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden in Abyan, driving people to the gathering place, staying with them when they rest." [213] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/259, no. 38645.]]

Hudhayfa said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the smoke? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then recited this verse: "The day the heaven brings a manifest smoke, covering the people; this is a painful punishment" [44:10–11]. It will fill what is between the east and the west, remaining forty days and nights. As for the believer, it will afflict him like a cold; as for the disbeliever, it will be like the state of a drunkard, coming out of his nostrils, ears and rear.

And with this chain from Ibn Jarir: Ya'qub related to us: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulayka, who said: I went to Ibn Abbas one day, and he said: I did not sleep last night until morning. I said: Why? He said: They said: the comet with a tail has risen, and I feared that the smoke had come by night, so I did not sleep until morning.

"Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers." How can they have the reminder (anna lahumu al-dhikra): from where would they have remembrance and admonition after the coming of the trial and the descent of punishment? "And there had already come to them a clear Messenger" (Muhammad, ﷺ). "Then they turned away from him and said: 'Taught, a man is teaching him,' 'a madman.'" "Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return to your disbelief." Qatadah said: "You will return to the punishment of Allah."

"On the day We seize with the greatest seizure": it is the day of Badr. "Indeed We will take retribution": this is the view of most scholars. Al-Hasan said: it is the Day of Resurrection.

It is reported from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "the greatest" is the day of Badr, and I say it is the Day of Resurrection.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 44, verses 17–37:**

﴿And We certainly tested before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger﴾ — this is Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him). It is said: "noble" means honored with Allah, and "esteemed and well-regarded among his people." ﴿Deliver to me the servants of Allah﴾ — meaning the Children of Israel, so that He would not punish them. ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾ — trustworthy in conveying the revelation.

﴿And do not exalt yourselves over Allah﴾ — meaning do not transgress and rebel, ﴿against Allah﴾, so that you disobey Him and oppose His command. ﴿Indeed, I bring you a clear authority﴾ — a manifest proof. Then they threatened him with killing. He said: ﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me﴾ — meaning, kill me. Qatada said: "stone me" means with stones. Ibn Abbas said: they would revile him and say, "He is a sorcerer." ﴿And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone﴾ — so let me go my way, unstoned by tongue or hand.

﴿So he called upon his Lord: "These are a criminal people"﴾ — meaning polytheists. Then He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So set out with My servants by night; indeed, you will be pursued﴾ — pursued by Pharaoh and his people.

﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾ — when you have crossed it, you and your companions, leaving it rahwan, still, in the state and condition in which it was when you entered it. ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned.﴾

The expressions of the exegetes differed concerning the meaning of rahw. Al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿rahwan﴾ that he said: "Calm (samta)." Al-Awfi related from him: "It means to leave it as it was." Ka'b: "A path." Rabi': "Smooth." Dahhak: "Wide open." Ikrima: "Dry, with the water receded," and it is said, "cleared away." Qatada: "A dry path." The original meaning of rahw in the speech of the Arabs is stillness. The poet said:

*As if the people of Hajr are looking, waiting to see me come out as a bird, ...*
*A bird that saw a falcon, its blood spilled upon it,*
*And its mother went out calmly (rahwan) to a festival.*

That is, "upon it, stillness."

﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station (maqam karim)﴾ — a noble gathering. It was called "noble" only because it was the gathering place of kings. This was said by Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who added: it means the pulpits. Qatada said: "noble" means fine. ﴿And luxury in which they had been delighting﴾ — comfortable, delighting, exulting, boastful, self-impressed. ﴿Thus, and We made others inherit them﴾ — the Children of Israel. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit﴾ [Al-A'raf 137], etc.

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾. This is because when a believer dies, the heaven and the earth weep over him for forty mornings. Ata said regarding this verse: their weeping is the redness of its horizons. Al-Suddi said: when al-Husayn ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) was killed, the heaven wept over him, and its weeping was its redness.

Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "They told us that the redness which is with the twilight had not existed until al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) was killed."

Ibn Bakr al-Khwarazmi informed us: Abu al-Ayyad al-Di'uli narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Khuthayma narrated to us, and from him, Abu Khuthayma narrated to us, Abu Salama narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, Sulaym al-Qadi informed us, who said: "It rained blood on the days when al-Husayn was killed."

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Ali al-Muqri narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Basri narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubayda al-Ramdhani narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqashi informed me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no servant except that he has two doors in the heaven: a door from which his provision descends, and a door through which his deeds and words ascend. When he dies, they miss him and weep over him," and he recited this verse: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾.

That is because they had not done any righteous deed on earth for which it would weep over them, and no good word or righteous deed had ascended to heaven from their speech or their deeds, so that it would miss them and weep.

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us: that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, Yahya ibn Talha narrated to us, Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd al-Hadrami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Islam began as a stranger and will return as a stranger. Beware, there is no estrangement for a believer. No believer dies in a foreign land where his mourners are absent, except that the heaven and the earth weep over him." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾, then said: "Indeed, the two do not weep over a disbeliever."

﴿And they were not given respite.﴾

﴿And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment﴾ — the slaughter of sons and the sparing of women — ﴿from Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty among the transgressors.﴾ ﴿And We certainly chose them﴾ — meaning the believers among the Children of Israel — ﴿with knowledge from Us﴾ — concerning them — ﴿over the worlds﴾ — meaning the worlds of their time. ﴿And We gave them of the signs that contained a manifest trial﴾. Qatada said: a clear blessing, when He split the sea for them, shaded them with clouds, and sent down upon them manna and quails.

Ibn Zayd said: He tested them with ease and hardship, and he recited: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned﴾ [Al-Anbiya 35].

﴿Indeed, these (i.e., the polytheists of Makkah)﴾ ﴿will surely say: "It is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected"﴾ — meaning, we will not be raised after our death. ﴿So bring our forefathers who have died, if you should be truthful﴾ — that we will be resurrected alive after death.

﴿Are they better, or the people of Tubba'?﴾ Qatada said: he is Tubba' al-Himyari, who marched with armies until he confused the people, built Samarqand, and whenever he wrote, he wrote in the name of the One who owns the land, sea, the morning, and the wind.

It has been mentioned to us that Ka'b used to say: Allah condemned his people but did not condemn him. A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) used to say: "Do not revile Tubba', for he was a righteous man." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he is the one who clothed the House (the Ka'ba).

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Qati'i narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Abu Zur'a Amr ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Do not revile Tubba', for he had indeed accepted Islam."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ali Salim al-Hamadhani narrated to us, Abu al-Azhar Ahmad ibn al-Azhar al-Nishapuri narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not know whether Tubba' was a prophet or not."

﴿And those before them﴾ — from the bygone disbelieving nations. ﴿We destroyed them; indeed, they were criminals.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: they would revile him and say, "He is a sorcerer." ﴿And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone﴾ — so let me go my way, unstoned by tongue or hand.

﴿So he called upon his Lord: "These are a criminal people"﴾ — meaning polytheists. Then He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So set out with My servants by night; indeed, you will be pursued﴾ — pursued by Pharaoh and his people.

﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾ — when you have crossed it, you and your companions, leaving it rahwan, still, in the state and condition in which it was when you entered it. ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned.﴾

The expressions of the exegetes differed concerning the meaning of rahw. Al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿rahwan﴾ that he said: "Calm (samta)." Al-Awfi related from him: "It means to leave it as it was." Ka'b: "A path." Rabi': "Smooth." Dahhak: "Wide open." Ikrima: "Dry, with the water receded," and it is said, "cleared away." Qatada: "A dry path." The original meaning of rahw in the speech of the Arabs is stillness. The poet said:

*As if the people of Hajr are looking, waiting to see me come out as a bird, ...*
*A bird that saw a falcon, its blood spilled upon it,*
*And its mother went out calmly (rahwan) to a festival.*

That is, "upon it, stillness."

﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station (maqam karim)﴾ — a noble gathering. It was called "noble" only because it was the gathering place of kings. This was said by Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who added: it means the pulpits. Qatada said: "noble" means fine. ﴿And luxury in which they had been delighting﴾ — comfortable, delighting, exulting, boastful, self-impressed. ﴿Thus, and We made others inherit them﴾ — the Children of Israel. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit﴾ [Al-A'raf 137], etc.

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾. This is because when a believer dies, the heaven and the earth weep over him for forty mornings. Ata said regarding this verse: their weeping is the redness of its horizons. Al-Suddi said: when al-Husayn ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) was killed, the heaven wept over him, and its weeping was its redness.

Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "They told us that the redness which is with the twilight had not existed until al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) was killed."

Ibn Bakr al-Khwarazmi informed us: Abu al-Ayyad al-Di'uli narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Khuthayma narrated to us, and from him, Abu Khuthayma narrated to us, Abu Salama narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, Sulaym al-Qadi informed us, who said: "It rained blood on the days when al-Husayn was killed."

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Ali al-Muqri narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Basri narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubayda al-Ramdhani narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqashi informed me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no servant except that he has two doors in the heaven: a door from which his provision descends, and a door through which his deeds and words ascend. When he dies, they miss him and weep over him," and he recited this verse: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾.

That is because they had not done any righteous deed on earth for which it would weep over them, and no good word or righteous deed had ascended to heaven from their speech or their deeds, so that it would miss them and weep.

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us: that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, Yahya ibn Talha narrated to us, Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd al-Hadrami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Islam began as a stranger and will return as a stranger. ﴿And they were not given respite.﴾

﴿And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment﴾ — the slaughter of sons and the sparing of women — ﴿from Pharaoh. Qatada said: a clear blessing, when He split the sea for them, shaded them with clouds, and sent down upon them manna and quails.

Ibn Zayd said: He tested them with ease and hardship, and he recited: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned﴾ [Al-Anbiya 35].

﴿Indeed, these (i.e., the polytheists of Makkah)﴾ ﴿will surely say: "It is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected"﴾ — meaning, we will not be raised after our death. ﴿So bring our forefathers who have died, if you should be truthful﴾ — that we will be resurrected alive after death.

﴿Are they better, or the people of Tubba'?﴾ Qatada said: he is Tubba' al-Himyari, who marched with armies until he confused the people, built Samarqand, and whenever he wrote, he wrote in the name of the One who owns the land, sea, the morning, and the wind.

It has been mentioned to us that Ka'b used to say: Allah condemned his people but did not condemn him. A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) used to say: "Do not revile Tubba', for he was a righteous man." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he is the one who clothed the House (the Ka'ba).

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Qati'i narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Abu Zur'a Amr ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Do not revile Tubba', for he had indeed accepted Islam."

﴿And those before them﴾ — from the bygone disbelieving nations. ﴿We destroyed them; indeed, they were criminals.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 44, verse 38–59:

﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in sport. We did not create them except with truth, but most of them do not know. Indeed, the Day of Judgement is the appointed time for them all, the Day when no close friend will avail another close friend at all, nor will they be helped, except for those on whom Allah has mercy.﴾ Ibn 'Amm does not repel on behalf of Ibn 'Ammih, nor does a friend on behalf of his friend.

﴿Nor will they be helped, except for him on whom Allah has mercy.﴾ The grammarians differed regarding the position (mahall) of (مَنْ, man). Some of them said: its position is nominative, as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in (يُنْصَرُونَ, yunsarun). If you wish, you may make it an inchoative (mubtada') and supply its predicate, meaning: ﴿except for him on whom Allah has mercy﴾, so we will suffice for him and intercede for him. And if you wish, you may make it accusative as an exception of disjunction (istithna' munqati') from the beginning of the speech, meaning: "O Allah, except for him on whom Allah has mercy." ﴿Indeed He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinner﴾, meaning the wicked one, who is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Aqil ibn Hamd informed me: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir narrated to me: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said: Abu al-Darda' was teaching a man, ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinner﴾, and the man began to say "the food of the orphan" (ṭa'ām al-yatīm). When he repeated it to him, Abu al-Darda' saw that he did not understand, and said: "Say: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the wicked one.﴾"

﴿Like molten brass (al-muhl), it boils﴾ — Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ruways read (يَغْلِي, yaghli) with the ya', while the others read it with the ta' (تَغْلِي), making the verb feminine due to the feminine nature of the tree (al-shajara).

﴿In the bellies, like the boiling of scalding water.﴾ ﴿Seize him﴾, meaning the sinner; ﴿then drag him﴾, i.e., push him, thrust him, and drive him to the Fire. It is said: "ʿatalahu, yaʿtiluhu, ʿatlan," when he drives him with violence, pushing and pulling. Al-Farazdaq said:

"The noble ones are not with us, your fathers, until you are dragged to ʿAṭiyya."

That is, driven by pushing and dragging. In it there are two dialects: with a kasra on the ta' (تَعْتِلُ, ta'tilu), which is the reading of Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Amr and the people of Kufa, and with a damma, which is the reading of the rest.

﴿To the midst of the Blazing Fire. Then pour over his head some of the torment of scalding water.﴾ This is the water of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 19]. Then it is said to him: ﴿Taste this! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ among your people, ﴿by your own claim.﴾ That is because Abu Jahl said: "Between its two mountains there is no man mightier or more noble than I." The guards say this to him in a manner of mockery and rebuke.

The common reading is (إِنَّكَ, innaka) with a kasra on the alif, as an inchoative. Al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha, in the sense of (لِأَنَّكَ, la'annaka), "because you."

﴿Indeed, this is what you used to doubt﴾, i.e., you used to be skeptical and did not believe in it, but now you have encountered it, so taste it. ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in a secure place﴾. The people of Medina and Syria read (مَقامٍ, maqam) with a damma on the mim, as a verbal noun, meaning "in a dwelling"; others read it with a fatha, meaning "in a noble place."

﴿In gardens and springs. They will wear fine silk and brocade, facing one another.﴾ Sundus is what is thin of brocade; istabraq is what is thick of it, an arabized word. ﴿Thus﴾, and just as We honored them with the gardens, the springs, and the garments, thus We honored them by ﴿We will marry them to Hur (al-'In)﴾, who are the pure, very white women. Mujahid said: "The gaze is dazzled by their whiteness and the clarity of their complexion, their shins visible through their garments, and the beholder sees his face in the liver of one of them like a mirror, due to the thinness of the skin and the clarity of the color."

The evidence for this interpretation is that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is (بِعِيسٍ عِينٍ), and they are the white ones; from this the white camels are called ʿīs, its singular being ba'ir a'yas and naqa ʿaysa'. It is also said: al-Hur are those intensely white in the whites of the eyes and intensely black in the pupils; their singular is aḥwar, and al-ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynā', which is one with large eyes.

Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Tabari al-Hajji informed us: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Isma'il ibn Khalaf al-Khayyat narrated to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yu'la Abu Ali al-Kufi narrated to us: Umar ibn Subayh narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The dowry of the Hur al-'In is handfuls of dates and pieces of bread."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Habash: Abd Allah ibn Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us: Ayyub ibn Ali, that is al-Sabahi, narrated to us: Ziyad ibn Sayyar, my client, narrated to us, from ʿIzza bint Abi Qarsafa, from her father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Removing the rubbish from the mosque is the dowry of the Hur al-'In."

﴿They will call for every kind of fruit they desire, secure﴾ from their running out or their absence at some times, and from their harm and injury. Qatada said: "Secure from death, ailments, and Satan."

﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾, meaning apart from the first death, and after it. This is like saying in speech: "I have not tasted food today except what I ate yesterday."

﴿And He protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire, as a bounty from your Lord. The evidence for this interpretation is that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is (بِعِيسٍ عِينٍ), and they are the white ones; from this the white camels are called ʿīs, its singular being ba'ir a'yas and naqa ʿaysa'. It is also said: al-Hur are those intensely white in the whites of the eyes and intensely black in the pupils; their singular is aḥwar, and al-ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynā', which is one with large eyes.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Habash: Abd Allah ibn Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us: Ayyub ibn Ali, that is al-Sabahi, narrated to us: Ziyad ibn Sayyar, my client, narrated to us, from ʿIzza bint Abi Qarsafa, from her father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Removing the rubbish from the mosque is the dowry of the Hur al-'In."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 44, verse 38–59:

﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in sport. We did not create them except with truth, but most of them do not know. Indeed, the Day of Judgement is the appointed time for them all, the Day when no close friend will avail another close friend at all, nor will they be helped, except for those on whom Allah has mercy.﴾ Ibn 'Amm does not repel on behalf of Ibn 'Ammih, nor does a friend on behalf of his friend.

﴿Nor will they be helped, except for him on whom Allah has mercy.﴾ The grammarians differed regarding the position (mahall) of (مَنْ, man). Some of them said: its position is nominative, as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in (يُنْصَرُونَ, yunsarun). If you wish, you may make it an inchoative (mubtada') and supply its predicate, meaning: ﴿except for him on whom Allah has mercy﴾, so we will suffice for him and intercede for him. And if you wish, you may make it accusative as an exception of disjunction (istithna' munqati') from the beginning of the speech, meaning: "O Allah, except for him on whom Allah has mercy." ﴿Indeed He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinner﴾, meaning the wicked one, who is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Aqil ibn Hamd informed me: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir narrated to me: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said: Abu al-Darda' was teaching a man, ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinner﴾, and the man began to say "the food of the orphan" (ṭa'ām al-yatīm). When he repeated it to him, Abu al-Darda' saw that he did not understand, and said: "Say: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the wicked one.﴾"

﴿Like molten brass (al-muhl), it boils﴾ — Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ruways read (يَغْلِي, yaghli) with the ya', while the others read it with the ta' (تَغْلِي), making the verb feminine due to the feminine nature of the tree (al-shajara).

﴿In the bellies, like the boiling of scalding water.﴾ ﴿Seize him﴾, meaning the sinner; ﴿then drag him﴾, i.e., push him, thrust him, and drive him to the Fire. It is said: "ʿatalahu, yaʿtiluhu, ʿatlan," when he drives him with violence, pushing and pulling. Al-Farazdaq said:

"The noble ones are not with us, your fathers, until you are dragged to ʿAṭiyya."

That is, driven by pushing and dragging. In it there are two dialects: with a kasra on the ta' (تَعْتِلُ, ta'tilu), which is the reading of Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Amr and the people of Kufa, and with a damma, which is the reading of the rest.

﴿To the midst of the Blazing Fire. Then pour over his head some of the torment of scalding water.﴾ This is the water of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 19]. Then it is said to him: ﴿Taste this! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ among your people, ﴿by your own claim.﴾ That is because Abu Jahl said: "Between its two mountains there is no man mightier or more noble than I." The guards say this to him in a manner of mockery and rebuke.

The common reading is (إِنَّكَ, innaka) with a kasra on the alif, as an inchoative. Al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha, in the sense of (لِأَنَّكَ, la'annaka), "because you."
